WF-02 STEP 2c SECURITY GATE -- REQ-027 -- VERDICT: PASS.

Gated `git diff origin/main...HEAD` on feature/WF02-REQ027-20260816 (implementation commit 093b114; 16 files, +2360/-9). Application-code surface actually reviewed: priv/repo/migrations/20260816193001_create_process_definitions.exs, priv/repo/migrations/20260816193002_create_instance_definition_snapshots.exs, lib/letflow/definitions/process_definition.ex, lib/letflow/definitions/instance_definition_snapshot.ex, and a comment/manifest/@doc-only change to lib/letflow/tenant_provisioning.ex. Everything else in the diff is bookkeeping (handoffs/, docs/issues/, docs/status/, docs/requirements.yaml) plus the 1295-line design artefact. The diff listing in the dispatch prompt was verified against the actual diff, not taken on trust.

=== 1. SCOPE TEST -- IN SCOPE (re-derived, not inherited from ORCH) ===

ORCH's assessment was IN SCOPE. I re-derived it independently and reach the same verdict, on three of the five triggers in .claude/agents/security-reviewer.md's scope test:

  * "Adds/modifies a priv/repo/migrations/*.exs migration" -- YES, two new files, both creating business tables (process_definitions, instance_definition_snapshots). This alone is dispositive.
  * "Adds/modifies response-shaping code for a tenant-scoped entity" -- partially: two new Ecto.Schema modules defining the field set of tenant-scoped entities, including a tenant_id column and a created_by actor-identity column. No serialisation layer is added (see INV-2 below), but the field set these modules declare is what a future response would be shaped from.
  * "a lookup-by-ID handler" -- NO (verified empirically, see INV-5).
  * API route / secret resolution -- NO.

Additionally the diff appends two entries to Letflow.TenantProvisioning's @tenant_scoped_migration_manifest, i.e. to the migration-replay path that interpolates a tenant schema name into DDL. That is a tenant-isolation-critical path even though the diff changes no line of the interpolation itself.

VERDICT: IN SCOPE. Full INV-1..INV-8 checklist run below. Not one invariant was silently skipped.

=== 2. INV-1..INV-8 DETERMINATION TABLE ===

  INV-1  Tenant data isolation .............................. APPLIES        -> PASS
  INV-2  Server-side field authorisation .................... NOT-APPLICABLE
  INV-3  Untrusted runtime sandboxing ....................... NOT-APPLICABLE
  INV-4  Secrets by reference only .......................... APPLIES        -> PASS
  INV-5  Not-found/forbidden indistinguishability ........... NOT-APPLICABLE
  INV-6  New data-access paths prove their scoping .......... APPLIES        -> PASS
  INV-7  No SQL string interpolation ........................ APPLIES        -> PASS
  INV-8  No unhandled crashes on realistic failure paths .... APPLIES        -> PASS

No applicable invariant failed. All are BLOCKER severity; there is no partial credit and none was taken.

=== 3. INV-1 -- TENANT DATA ISOLATION -- APPLIES, PASS ===

APPLICABILITY. The role file's generic guidance says INV-1's verdict "today is almost always NOT-APPLICABLE" because it is written for S1/S4/S5. That guidance is superseded here by security-invariants.md itself, which is the AUTHORITATIVE file ("Where this file and any other doc disagree, this file wins") and whose INV-1 "How to verify" states the precondition explicitly: "Not yet checkable -- becomes checkable once 0003 lands and S2/S3 migrations exist." Both halves are now true -- docs/migration/decisions/0003-ecto-schema-strategy.md is `Status: decided (REQ-012)`, and this handoff's context.stage is S2 with two S2 business-table migrations in the diff. INV-1's own Severity line agrees: "BLOCKER (once S1/S2 land)". So INV-1 APPLIES. This matches the determination the REQ-023 and REQ-024 Step 2c runs reached on the same reasoning (checked after deriving it independently, not before).

INV-1 requires confirming (a) every new Ecto schema module scopes its queries through the chosen tenancy mechanism, and (b) that no migration creates a business table reachable outside that mechanism. Both were verified against a live Postgres (letflow_test2, MIX_TEST_PARTITION=2), not by reading the code alone.

(b) NO BUSINESS TABLE IS REACHABLE OUTSIDE THE MECHANISM. `MIX_ENV=test MIX_TEST_PARTITION=2 mix ecto.migrate` (a plain, prefix-less run -- the exact scenario the `if prefix() do` guard exists for) reports "Migrations already up", and a catalogue read of the public schema afterwards shows neither table there:

    === STEP 1. After a plain `mix ecto.migrate` (NO prefix): are the two new tables in `public`? ===
      public.process_definitions exists? false   (expected: false -- the `if prefix() do` guard)
      public.instance_definition_snapshots exists? false   (expected: false -- the `if prefix() do` guard)
      full public table list: ["approvals", "groups", "schema_migrations", "tenant_role", "tenant_schemas", "tenants", "transition_events", "users"]

The public schema contains only the structurally-global tables (tenants, tenant_schemas, the REQ-015 identity tables, schema_migrations, and the two pre-S2 MVP tables). Neither REQ-027 table leaked into it.

Then a real tenant was provisioned and the manifest replayed:

    === STEP 2. Provision a tenant schema and replay the 9-entry manifest ===
    CREATE SCHEMA IF NOT EXISTS "tenant_a7fab13d10a1477fa411ec95aa0deb05" []
      provisioned schema_name = "tenant_a7fab13d10a1477fa411ec95aa0deb05"
      replay_migrations/2 applied versions = [20260816120001, 20260816120002, 20260816120003, 20260816120004, 20260816120005, 20260816120006, 20260816163103, 20260816193001, 20260816193002]

    === STEP 3. Placement: tenant schema vs public ===
      tenant_a7fab13d10a1477fa411ec95aa0deb05.process_definitions exists? true  |  public.process_definitions exists? false
      tenant_a7fab13d10a1477fa411ec95aa0deb05.instance_definition_snapshots exists? true  |  public.instance_definition_snapshots exists? false

Both new versions (20260816193001, 20260816193002) are selected by the manifest and both tables land inside the tenant's own Postgres schema and nowhere else. The two halves REQ-022 requires (guard in the file + registration in the manifest) are both present; a guarded-but-unregistered migration would be inert, a registered-but-unguarded one would corrupt public, and neither failure mode is present.

The foreign key does NOT cross the tenant boundary -- it resolves inside the same tenant schema, so no snapshot row can reference another tenant's definition:

    === STEP 7. Does the FK cross the tenant-schema boundary? ===
      FOREIGN KEY (definition_id) REFERENCES tenant_a7fab13d10a1477fa411ec95aa0deb05.process_definitions(id)

(a) BOTH SCHEMA MODULES SCOPE THROUGH THE MECHANISM. Verified against the compiled modules rather than their moduledocs:

    PD    __schema__(:source) = "process_definitions"
    PD    __schema__(:prefix) = nil
    IDS   __schema__(:source) = "instance_definition_snapshots"
    IDS   __schema__(:prefix) = nil

Neither declares an @schema_prefix. Under Decision B that is the correct and safer shape: a compile-time prefix would hardcode one tenant, whereas nil forces every read/write to pass `prefix: schema_name` at call time. I verified the resulting failure mode is loud, not silent -- a query that forgets the prefix does not read another tenant's rows, it fails to resolve the relation at all:

    === STEP 9. Cross-schema read attempt with NO prefix (the Decision B fail-loud property) ===
      Repo.all(ProcessDefinition) with no prefix: {:raised, Postgrex.Error, :undefined_table}

This is exactly the blast-radius property 0003 Decision B cites as its reason for choosing schema-per-tenant over a tenant_id predicate on shared tables ("a bug that forgets a tenant_id predicate ... fails loudly ... instead of silently leaking rows"). Demonstrated here, not assumed.

Finally, neither module exposes any query/lookup function that could bypass the prefix -- see the INV-5 evidence below, where __info__(:functions) shows only changeset builders.

INV-1 RESULT: PASS.

=== 4. INV-2 -- SERVER-SIDE FIELD AUTHORISATION -- NOT-APPLICABLE ===

S4 has not started and this diff adds no response-shaping surface. Verified rather than assumed -- greping every ADDED line in lib/ and priv/ for serialisation constructs:

    === INV-2: any serialisation / response-shaping introduced by this diff? ===
    git diff origin/main...HEAD -- lib/ priv/ | grep -E '^\+' | grep -nE 'Jason|derive|@derive|Encoder|render|json\(|put_resp|conn\b'
    676:+  table's prefix (`connection.ex:1339` renders `quote_name(index.prefix, index.table)`
    1775:+# default type is `:bigserial` (migration.ex:513), which the adapter renders as

Both hits are the English word "renders" inside design-doc/migration-comment prose. Zero Jason.Encoder derivations, zero view modules, zero conn handling. Nothing is serialised, so there is no field-selection point to audit. NOT-APPLICABLE.

Worth recording for the requirement that does add a response surface: process_definitions carries `created_by` (actor identity) and `tenant_id`, and instance_definition_snapshots carries a full captured `graph`. Whichever requirement first serialises these entities is where INV-2 becomes live, and the field list is now fixed by these two modules.

=== 5. INV-3 -- UNTRUSTED RUNTIME SANDBOXING -- NOT-APPLICABLE ===

S5 (scripting/plugins) has not started, and per security-invariants.md INV-3's own "How to verify" the check is "Deferred until S5's decision record exists" -- no such record exists. Verified the diff introduces no script/plugin/native surface:

    786:+| `idx_snap_definition` | ... must sequentially scan this table to evaluate the FK's `NO ACTION` check ...
    1847:+      # DELETE FROM process_definitions must sequentially scan this table to evaluate the

Note the `graph` column is tenant-authored JSON, but REQ-027 stores it and never executes it; PD-02 structural validation is REQ-028's Letflow.Definitions.Graph and no evaluation path is added here. INV-3 becomes relevant only if a future requirement executes graph content.

=== 6. INV-4 -- SECRETS BY REFERENCE ONLY -- APPLIES, PASS ===

APPLICABILITY. The diff resolves no secret, so the narrow scope-test trigger ("adds/modifies anything resolving a secret") is not met. I still treat INV-4 as APPLIES rather than NOT-APPLICABLE for two reasons: security-invariants.md states plainly "Applies now -- this is the one invariant already relevant at MVP-1/S0 scale", and INV-4's rule explicitly covers serialisation into "any payload -- API response, audit record, webhook body, or handoff file", and this diff adds four handoff files plus two issue records. Calling it NOT-APPLICABLE would be the cheaper but weaker call.

DOCUMENTED CHECK, RUN AS WRITTEN:

    $ grep -rn "System.get_env" config/ lib/ --include=*.ex
    lib/letflow/application.ex:38:  defp skip_migrations?, do: System.get_env("RELEASE_NAME") == nil

    $ grep -rniE "(password|secret|client_secret|token)\s*=\s*\"[^\"]{8,}" lib/ config/ --include=*.ex
    (no output, exit 1)

ISS-0018 COMPENSATION -- MANDATORY, NOT OPTIONAL. Both documented greps pass `--include=*.ex` while naming config/ as a search root. I confirmed the defect is real before compensating for it, rather than taking ISS-0018 on trust:

    $ ls config/
    config.exs  dev.exs  prod.exs  runtime.exs  test.exs

Every file in config/ is `.exs`, so `--include=*.ex` matches none of them and INV-4's own primary cited target (config/dev.exs's REQ-103 bearer-token pattern) is structurally invisible to INV-4's own check. An empty result set from those commands is therefore not evidence of anything. Supplementary passes with `--include=*.exs` added:

    $ grep -rn "System.get_env" config/ lib/ --include=*.ex --include=*.exs
    config/runtime.exs:11:    System.get_env("DATABASE_URL") ||
    config/runtime.exs:19:    pool_size: String.to_integer(System.get_env("POOL_SIZE") || "10")
    config/test.exs:6:  database: "letflow_test#{System.get_env("MIX_TEST_PARTITION")}",

    $ grep -rniE "(password|secret|client_secret|token)\s*=\s*\"[^\"]{8,}" lib/ config/ --include=*.ex --include=*.exs
    (no output, exit 1)

    $ grep -rniE "(password|secret|client_secret|api_key|token)[\"']?\s*[:=]+\s*[\"'][^\"']{8,}" lib/ config/

The third is a broadened sweep I added because the documented pattern only matches `=`-assignment and would miss Elixir's far more common `key: "value"` keyword form -- the shape config/*.exs actually uses. It also drops the --include filter entirely so no extension can hide. Still clean.

MANUAL CONFIRMATION (the documented check requires it). The one credential-shaped literal in the tree is config/dev.exs:9 / config/test.exs:5 `password: "letflow"` -- a 7-character local docker-compose Postgres credential, below the greps' {8,} threshold and matching docker-compose.yml. It is a local dev fixture, not secret material, it predates this branch, and this diff does not touch config/ at all (confirmed from `git diff --stat`, which lists no config/ path). config/runtime.exs resolves DATABASE_URL from the environment at point of use and raises if absent -- exactly INV-4's prescribed pattern. The OIDC block in config/dev.exs carries a `client_id` but deliberately no `client_secret`, with an in-file comment explaining the plug is a resource server that never performs a token exchange.

DIFF-LOCAL CHECK: the two new schema modules and two new migrations contain no env access, no token, no credential, and nothing that could serialise one. The four handoff files and two issue records added by the diff contain no secret material.

INV-4 RESULT: PASS.

=== 7. INV-5 -- NOT-FOUND/FORBIDDEN INDISTINGUISHABILITY -- NOT-APPLICABLE ===

Deferred until S4 per INV-5's own "How to verify". Verified independently that the diff adds no lookup-by-ID endpoint and, more strongly, that neither new module exposes any lookup function at all. From __info__(:functions) on the compiled modules:

    === ProcessDefinition.__info__(:functions) ===
      __changeset__/0  __schema__/1  __schema__/2  __struct__/0  __struct__/1
      create_changeset/2  update_changeset/2

    === InstanceDefinitionSnapshot.__info__(:functions) ===
      __changeset__/0  __schema__/1  __schema__/2  __struct__/0  __struct__/1
      create_changeset/2

Only changeset builders; no get/1, no fetch/1, no query function, no controller. And the router/plug surface is untouched:

    $ git diff --stat origin/main...HEAD -- lib/letflow_web/ lib/letflow/router.ex lib/letflow/plugs/ web/
    (no output)

There is no code path that can distinguish "exists, not yours" from "never existed" because there is no lookup path. NOT-APPLICABLE.

=== 8. INV-6 -- NEW DATA-ACCESS PATHS PROVE THEIR SCOPING -- APPLIES, PASS ===

APPLIES on its own terms: "a new migration introducing a business table" -- two of them. INV-6's "How to verify" is that a SECURITY-REVIEWER handoff exists for the change with status PASS whose result explicitly lists which of INV-1..INV-8 were assessed and why each applies-and-is-satisfied or does-not-apply. This handoff is that artefact: section 2's table gives all eight determinations, and each APPLIES invariant has its documented check actually executed with real output quoted above and below. The satisfaction is not "it compiles and the happy-path test passes" -- it is the live-Postgres catalogue evidence in section 3 showing both tables exist only inside a tenant schema, plus the demonstrated undefined_table failure for an unprefixed query.

INV-6 RESULT: PASS.

=== 9. INV-7 -- NO SQL STRING INTERPOLATION -- APPLIES, PASS ===

DOCUMENTED CHECK, RUN AS WRITTEN:

    $ grep -rn "Repo.query" lib/ priv/repo/migrations/ --include=*.ex --include=*.exs
    lib/letflow/tenant_provisioning.ex:109:          Repo.query!("SELECT pg_advisory_xact_lock(hashtext($1))", [schema_name])
    lib/letflow/tenant_provisioning.ex:123:          Repo.query!(~s(CREATE SCHEMA IF NOT EXISTS "#{schema_name}"))

Two hits, both pre-existing REQ-022 code, manually confirmed as the check requires:

  * :109 is fully parameterised -- $1 with a bind list. No interpolation.
  * :123 is the codebase's only raw-SQL identifier interpolation. Postgres cannot bind a DDL identifier as a parameter, so interpolation is the only available mechanism; safety comes from schema_name's constrained shape.

THE DIFF INTRODUCES NO NEW INTERPOLATION SITE. Filtering the tenant_provisioning.ex diff for any changed line touching interpolation, the prefix, or the DDL path:

    $ git diff origin/main...HEAD -- lib/letflow/tenant_provisioning.ex | grep -E "^[+-]" | grep -vE "^(\+\+\+|---)" \
        | grep -E "Repo.query|CREATE SCHEMA|schema_name_for_tenant|Ecto.UUID|Migrator.run|prefix:"
    (no output, exit 1)

Every changed line in that file is a comment, a @doc paragraph, or a manifest tuple. Neither Repo.query! call, nor schema_name_for_tenant/1, nor the Ecto.Migrator.run(..., prefix: schema_name) call is modified.

    $ git diff origin/main...HEAD -- lib/ priv/ | grep -E '^\+' | grep -nE '#\{'
    (5 hits: lines 412, 823, 895, 937, 1782 -- all `"#{table.name}_#{column}_fkey"` and
     `"#{version}_#{Macro.underscore(...)}.exs"` quoted INSIDE markdown prose or a migration
     comment, describing what Ecto itself does. Zero executable interpolation.)

    $ git diff origin/main...HEAD -- lib/ priv/ | grep -E '^\+' | grep -nE 'Repo\.query|Ecto\.Adapters\.SQL|execute\(|fragment\('
    (2 hits: a design-doc table row, and the single executable one --
     priv/repo/migrations/...create_instance_definition_snapshots.exs:106
       default: fragment("(now() AT TIME ZONE 'utc')")
     a compile-time constant string with no interpolation and no user input.)

Both migrations use the Ecto.Migration DSL exclusively -- create table/3, create index/3, create unique_index/3, references/2 -- all parameterised-by-construction. The two index predicates ("status = 'active'", "stage IS NOT NULL") are literal constants written by the developer, not interpolated values; confirmed in the emitted DDL:

    CREATE UNIQUE INDEX uq_active_definition ON tenant_a7fab.....process_definitions USING btree (name) WHERE ((status)::text = 'active'::text)
    CREATE INDEX idx_def_stage ON tenant_a7fab.....process_definitions USING btree (stage) WHERE (stage IS NOT NULL)

NO NEW PATH CAN REACH schema_name_for_tenant/1 WITH UNCONSTRAINED INPUT. `grep -rn "schema_name_for_tenant\|replay_migrations\|provision_tenant_schema" lib/ test/` shows every call site; filtering the diff's added lines for any of those three names returns only design-doc prose -- the diff adds zero new call sites. I re-confirmed REQ-023's structural finding empirically rather than inheriting it, firing injection payloads at the function:

    === schema_name_for_tenant/1 fired with injection payloads and edge cases ===
      in  = "a\"; DROP SCHEMA public CASCADE; --"                              out = {:error, :invalid_tenant_id}   -> REJECTED
      in  = "public\"; CREATE TABLE pwn(x int); --"                            out = {:error, :invalid_tenant_id}   -> REJECTED
      in  = "00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000\"; DROP TABLE tenants; --"   out = {:error, :invalid_tenant_id}   -> REJECTED
      in  = "tenant_x\" , \"y"                                                 out = {:error, :invalid_tenant_id}   -> REJECTED
      in  = " "                                                                out = {:error, :invalid_tenant_id}   -> REJECTED
      in  = "00000000-0000-0000-0000-00000000000"                              out = {:error, :invalid_tenant_id}   -> REJECTED
      in  = "0000000000000000000000000000000g"                                 out = {:error, :invalid_tenant_id}   -> REJECTED
      in  = "0000000000000000000000000000000A"                                 out = {:error, :invalid_tenant_id}   -> REJECTED
      in  = "0000000000000000000000000000ABCD"                                 out = {:error, :invalid_tenant_id}   -> REJECTED
      in  = "00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000"   out = {:ok, "tenant_00000000000000000000000000000000"}   -> SAFE (matches ^tenant_[0-9a-f]{32}$)
      in  = "AAAAAAAA-BBBB-CCCC-DDDD-EEEEEEEEEEEE"   out = {:ok, "tenant_aaaaaaaabbbbccccddddeeeeeeeeeeee"}   -> SAFE (matches ^tenant_[0-9a-f]{32}$)

Ecto.UUID.cast/1 rejects every payload carrying a quote, semicolon, comment marker or space, and lowercase-normalises valid input, so the only strings that survive match ^tenant_[0-9a-f]{32}$ and cannot terminate the quoted identifier at :123.

INV-7 RESULT: PASS.

=== 10. INV-8 -- NO UNHANDLED CRASHES ON REALISTIC FAILURE PATHS -- APPLIES, PASS ===

DOCUMENTED CHECK, RUN AS WRITTEN:

    $ grep -rn "^\s*{:ok, .*} = " lib/letflow/ --include=*.ex
    lib/letflow/event_store/registry.ex:248:          {:ok, %EventType{} = event_type} ->
    lib/letflow/identity.ex:171:      {:ok, %User{id: id} = inserted} ->
    lib/letflow/tenant_provisioning.ex:126:            {:ok, %Registration{} = registration} ->
    lib/letflow/tenant_provisioning.ex:303:      {:ok, %Registration{id: id} = inserted} ->

Four hits, all manually confirmed as the check requires, and all FALSE POSITIVES of the heuristic: every one is a `case ... do` CLAUSE HEAD, not a bare `=` match that can raise. The `= var` in each is an alias binding on a matched struct, and each has a complementary error clause in the same case -- registry.ex:248 pairs with `{:error, %Ecto.Changeset{} = failed_changeset} ->`, identity.ex:171 with its own error clause, tenant_provisioning.ex:126 with `{:error, :tenant_not_found} ->` and `{:error, %Ecto.Changeset{} = changeset} ->`, and :303 with `{:error, %Ecto.Changeset{} = changeset} ->`. A failing Repo.insert/2 lands in the error clause; nothing raises.

NONE OF THE FOUR IS INTRODUCED BY THIS DIFF. Supplementary passes over the diff's own new files:

    $ grep -rn "^\s*{:ok, .*} = " priv/repo/migrations/ --include=*.exs
    (no output, exit 1)
    $ grep -nE "^\s*(\{|%)" lib/letflow/definitions/process_definition.ex lib/letflow/definitions/instance_definition_snapshot.ex
    (no output, exit 1)

Both new modules are pure changeset builders that perform no I/O at all -- create_changeset/2 and update_changeset/2 only cast/validate. There is no external call, no network input and no tenant-controlled data reaching a bare match. The tenant_provisioning.ex change adds no executable statement (comments, @doc, manifest tuples only).

Both modules also do the INV-8-adjacent thing correctly on the error-shape axis: every DB constraint they rely on has a declared Ecto counterpart, so a violation surfaces as {:error, changeset} rather than a raised Ecto.ConstraintError -- unique_constraint on :uq_definition_version and :uq_active_definition, unique_constraint on :instance_definition_snapshots_pkey, and foreign_key_constraint on :instance_definition_snapshots_definition_id_fkey. I verified all four of those DB objects actually exist with exactly those names (section 3's pg_indexes/pg_constraint output), so no declaration is a dead string that would let a 23505/23503 escape as a raise.

INV-8 RESULT: PASS.

=== 11. ANSWER TO THE NOT-NULL QUESTION (beyond ISS-0025) ===

QUESTION: does shipping process_definitions.tenant_id as NOT NULL with no DB default, which nothing currently supplies, have any TENANT-ISOLATION consequence beyond the insert failure already recorded as ISS-0025?

VERDICT: NO. It is isolation-neutral today, and on the isolation axis specifically it is strictly SAFER than the alternatives -- including R-Co's own shape. It does not weaken INV-1 and is not a gate concern. This is not a restatement of ISS-0025, which frames the gap purely functionally; the reasoning below is on the isolation axis, and it reaches a different conclusion about the three candidate resolutions than ISS-0025 does.

FIRST DIRECTION -- is a never-populated column a latent isolation weakness? Does any INV-1 intra-schema query-predicate discipline depend on it being populated? No, and I checked rather than assumed:

  (a) NO SHIPPED CONSTRAINT OR INDEX REFERENCES tenant_id. From the live catalogue read (section 3, STEP 6), the complete index set across both tables is: process_definitions_pkey(id), uq_definition_version(name, version), uq_active_definition(name) WHERE status='active', idx_def_stage(stage) WHERE stage IS NOT NULL, idx_def_status(status), instance_definition_snapshots_pkey(instance_id), idx_snap_definition(definition_id). Not one leads with, or even mentions, tenant_id. This matters because it means no uniqueness domain is scoped by tenant_id, so an unpopulated or wrongly-populated value cannot widen or narrow any constraint's enforcement. The migration header states the reason and it holds under Decision B: tenant_id has at most one distinct value per schema, so a tenant-leading index degenerates to its non-tenant counterpart. No enforcement is lost by their absence.

  (b) NO QUERY PREDICATE EXISTS TO DEGRADE. The two modules expose only changeset builders (__info__(:functions) above); REQ-030 owns create/1 and every read, and is not built. There is no live `where: tenant_id == ^x` anywhere that could silently start matching nothing.

  (c) THE SIBLING TABLE PROVES THE POINT. instance_definition_snapshots carries NO tenant_id at all -- deliberately, per adp-02's table mapping -- yet is fully isolated: it lives inside the tenant schema and its FK resolves within that same schema (STEP 7 output). If tenant_id were load-bearing for isolation, this table would be unisolated, and it plainly is not. That is direct evidence the boundary is the Postgres schema, exactly as Decision B says.

  (d) THE MISSING-PREFIX FAILURE MODE IS INDEPENDENT OF tenant_id. STEP 9 shows an unprefixed query raises Postgrex.Error :undefined_table -- a relation-resolution failure, not a predicate failure. Populating or not populating tenant_id changes nothing about it.

SECOND DIRECTION -- is it isolation-neutral because the schema is the real boundary? Yes, and one step further: the shipped shape is the SAFEST of the available options on this axis, because the failure is a hard rejection rather than a silent wrong value. Verified empirically -- a raw INSERT omitting tenant_id, bypassing the changeset's validate_required so the DB constraint is what answers:

    === STEP 8. NOT NULL tenant_id with no default: what actually happens on an insert that omits it ===
      insert WITH tenant_id supplied: OK, id=e9af6343-..., tenant_id=a7fab13d-10a1-477f-a411-ec95aa0deb05, status=:draft
      raw INSERT omitting tenant_id: %Postgrex.Error{postgres: %{code: :not_null_violation,
        message: "null value in column \"tenant_id\" of relation \"process_definitions\" violates not-null constraint",
        table: "process_definitions", ...}}

Contrast the shape ISS-0025 notes R-Co uses -- NOT NULL plus a session-GUC DEFAULT (bpm_effective_tenant_id()). Under that design a connection whose GUC is unset or stale silently stamps rows with a wrong or reserved tenant UUID and no error is raised anywhere. Since 0003 Decision B's stated purpose for retaining tenant_id is cross-tenant admin/reporting queries run against a superuser connection -- i.e. queries that read ACROSS schemas and use tenant_id as the attribution field -- mis-stamped rows would misattribute one tenant's definitions to another in exactly the query class the column exists to serve. Letflow's no-default NOT NULL cannot produce that: it either gets a real value or it refuses the write. A nullable column would be worse still (silent NULLs, undetectable). So the constraint as shipped converts a would-be silent-corruption class into a loud, immediate, already-filed functional failure. That is the correct trade for a security gate.

FORWARD-LOOKING NOTE (new, not in ISS-0025 -- filed below as a MINOR observation). The isolation axis does discriminate between ISS-0025's three candidate resolutions, and ISS-0025 evaluates them only on API-shape and coupling grounds. Option (a) "caller supplies tenant_id" makes the value caller-controlled: nothing would then stop a write into tenant A's schema from carrying tenant_id = B. Reads stay safe (the schema boundary still holds), but the cross-tenant reporting query that trusts tenant_id -- the column's whole reason for existing -- would be corrupted, and silently. Option (b) session-GUC reintroduces the silent mis-stamp above. Option (c) deriving tenant_id from the prefix at write time is structurally incapable of disagreeing with the schema the row lands in, and is therefore the strongest on this axis. If (a) is chosen anyway, the writer must cross-check the supplied value against the prefix (schema_name_for_tenant(tenant_id) == prefix) rather than accept it unchecked. This is cheap to state now and expensive to retrofit after REQ-025 and REQ-030 have both shipped writers.

BOTTOM LINE: no isolation consequence beyond the recorded insert failure. INV-1 is not gated on tenant_id being populated, and REQ-027 is not blocked by ISS-0025.

=== 12. THE FK WITH NO ON DELETE CASCADE -- SECURITY ANALYSIS ===

Confirmed at the catalogue level, not from the moduledoc:

    === STEP 5. FK referential action (pg_constraint.confdeltype) ===
      instance_definition_snapshots_definition_id_fkey contype=f confdeltype="a" confupdtype="a"
        tenant_a7fab13d10a1477fa411ec95aa0deb05.instance_definition_snapshots -> "tenant_a7fab...".process_definitions

confdeltype='a' is NO ACTION, matching PD-08 and REQ-027 AC 4. Three security angles considered:

  DENIAL-OF-DELETION -- benign. Under NO ACTION a definition with any snapshot referencing it cannot be deleted (foreign_key_violation 23503), so an actor who starts an instance effectively pins that definition. But both rows live in the SAME tenant schema (STEP 7's constraint definition), so the pinning is strictly intra-tenant: no tenant can make another tenant's row undeletable. Within a tenant this is not a privilege boundary at all -- it is the intended durability guarantee (a snapshot must outlive attempts to remove its source). And no delete path ships in this diff: neither module exposes one (__info__(:functions)), and REQ-030 owns any future hard-delete. Not a security defect.

  DoS VIA EXPENSIVE FK CHECK -- ruled out. Postgres does not auto-index the referencing side of an FK, so an unindexed child table would force a sequential scan on every parent DELETE -- a genuine amplification vector as snapshot counts grow. idx_snap_definition(definition_id) is present and verified in the pg_indexes output, so the NO ACTION check is an index probe. The migration's own comment calls this out as load-bearing rather than decorative; the catalogue confirms it.

  ORPHAN RETENTION / ERASURE -- not an isolation concern. Because NO ACTION forbids deleting a referenced parent outright, no true orphan arises; the concern inverts into data retention (a definition cannot be hard-deleted while snapshots exist). Retained rows stay inside the tenant's own schema and are readable only through it, so nothing crosses a tenant boundary. Any right-to-erasure question this raises is a data-lifecycle policy matter for a later requirement, not INV-1/INV-2. I note it only so it is not lost: hard-erasure of a definition will require deciding what happens to its snapshots.

  The related wording defect in REQ-033's AC 4 is already ISS-0024 -- not re-filed.

=== 13. WRITE-ONCE (PD-08) -- CONSISTENT WITH REQ-027's SCOPE DIVISION ===

Verified against __info__(:functions) on the compiled module, NOT against the moduledoc's claim about itself:

    === InstanceDefinitionSnapshot.__info__(:functions) ===
      __changeset__/0  __schema__/1  __schema__/2  __struct__/0  __struct__/1  create_changeset/2

Only create_changeset/2. No update_changeset/2, no generic changeset/2, no delete function -- so the moduledoc's write-once claim is true as stated. Corroborating: __schema__(:associations) = [], so there is no belongs_to :definition to invite a preload across the snapshot->definition edge, which is the coupling PD-08 exists to break.

JUDGEMENT ON THE SCOPE DIVISION, not a defect finding. The absence of an update changeset is not runtime enforcement -- Ecto.Repo.update/2 and delete/2 act on structs and changesets and do not require a module-level function, so a determined caller could still mutate a snapshot row. That is not a REQ-027 defect: 0003 Decision C point 1 states immutability "is enforced at the application/context-module layer, not the migration layer", REQ-027's scope is schema only, and no context module (Letflow.Definitions.SnapshotStore, REQ-033) exists yet to enforce it. What shipped is exactly the schema-layer half of that division -- expose no mutation surface -- and it is consistent, so I judge it correct rather than treating the absent runtime enforcement as a gap. REQ-033 is where this becomes checkable, and a future Step 2c should verify it there.

=== 14. WHAT I DID NOT FIND ===

No cross-tenant leakage path. No table in public. No new SQL interpolation site. No new call site into schema_name_for_tenant/1. No secret material. No serialisation surface. No lookup-by-ID handler. No unhandled-crash path introduced. No hardcoded credential in the diff.

=== 15. ENVIRONMENT / CONSTRAINTS OBSERVED ===

All work in c:/Users/tvolo/dev/ai-dala/letflow-wt2 on branch feature/WF02-REQ027-20260816 (verified via git branch --show-current). No branch change, no docker compose up, no touch of the sibling worktree or ai-dala-infra. Every DB command ran with MIX_ENV=test MIX_TEST_PARTITION=2 against letflow_test2; letflow_test and letflow_dev were never touched. Both tenant schemas created during verification were dropped and their Registration/Tenant rows deleted; final state confirmed clean:

    === CLEANUP: dropped schema tenant_a7fab13d10a1477fa411ec95aa0deb05, deleted Registration + Tenant rows ===
      remaining tenant_* schemas in letflow_test2: []

Verification scripts were written to the session scratchpad outside the repo, so no stray file landed in the project tree; `git status --porcelain` shows only this handoff file. No application code was modified -- this is a gate.

issues.description: NEW (not ISS-0012..ISS-0025). Letflow.TenantProvisioning.Registration.changeset/2 (lib/letflow/tenant_provisioning/registration.ex) casts and requires :schema_name but applies no validate_format/3 constraining it to ^tenant_[0-9a-f]{32}$. Registration.schema_name is the value replay_migrations/2 passes as Ecto.Migrator.run/4's :prefix, which the Postgres adapter interpolates as a DDL/DML identifier -- so schema_name is an identifier-injection-relevant field, while the changeset that writes it treats it as free text. This is NOT exploitable today and is NOT a defect in REQ-027's diff: the only writer is TenantProvisioning.insert_or_fetch_registration/2, which is private and derives the value from schema_name_for_tenant/1 (re-verified this run: every injection payload is rejected by Ecto.UUID.cast/1, only ^tenant_[0-9a-f]{32}$ survives). The observation is that the constrained shape is guaranteed solely by the current call graph, not by the schema module that persists it, so any future public writer of a Registration row would silently remove the guarantee. The module's own @doc explicitly declines to re-implement that validation. A one-line validate_format/3 would make the invariant local to the data rather than to the caller. REQ-022 code, unchanged by this diff -- reported, not filed, per this run's instructions.

NEW dimension on the already-filed ISS-0025, not a re-file. ISS-0025 evaluates its three candidate resolutions for the unsatisfiable process_definitions.tenant_id NOT NULL purely on API-shape and coupling grounds. It does not evaluate them on the tenant-attribution-integrity axis, where they differ materially: option (a) 'caller supplies tenant_id' makes the value caller-controlled, so a row written into tenant A's Postgres schema could carry tenant_id = B with nothing rejecting it. Reads stay safe (the schema boundary still holds), but the cross-tenant admin/reporting query that 0003 Decision B cites as the column's whole reason for being retained would be silently misattributed. Option (b) session-GUC default reproduces R-Co's silent-mis-stamp risk when the GUC is unset or stale. Option (c) deriving tenant_id from the write prefix is structurally incapable of disagreeing with the schema the row lands in and is strongest on this axis. Recommendation to whoever resolves ISS-0025: if (a) is chosen, the writer must cross-check the supplied tenant_id against the prefix (schema_name_for_tenant(tenant_id) == prefix) rather than accept it unchecked. Cheap to state now, expensive to retrofit once REQ-025 and REQ-030 have both shipped writers. Suggested as an addendum to ISS-0025 rather than a separate issue.

ISS-0018 confirmed reproducing, with an additional facet worth recording on that issue. INV-4's two documented greps pass --include=*.ex while naming config/ as a search root; `ls config/` this run returned config.exs, dev.exs, prod.exs, runtime.exs, test.exs -- every file is .exs, so the commands structurally cannot inspect INV-4's own cited target and an empty result set proves nothing. Compensated for in this gate with --include=*.exs passes plus an unfiltered broadened sweep (all clean). ADDITIONAL FACET beyond ISS-0018's current text: the second grep's pattern also only matches `=`-assignment ((password|secret|...)\s*=\s*"..."), while Elixir config uses the keyword form `password: "..."` -- so even after the --include fix the pattern would still miss the shape config/ actually uses. Whoever fixes ISS-0018 should widen the operator class to [:=] as well as the file glob, otherwise the repaired check remains blind to its own primary target. Relatedly, the {8,} length threshold means config/dev.exs:9 / config/test.exs:5's `password: "letflow"` (7 chars) is invisible to the heuristic; that literal is a local docker-compose dev credential matching docker-compose.yml, not secret material, and is untouched by this diff -- noted only so the threshold's blind spot is on the record.
